title: Accept device-initiated Bluetooth Just Works pairing
head: 87c21cf5edde
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Default-agent registration reopens Pairable after the closed panel has cleared it
leads.consequence: With BlueZ 5.87's default AlwaysPairable=false, RequestDefaultAgent iterates adapters and enables the bondable/Pairable bit whenever the agent registers. If the shell has already loaded its closed panel and set Pairable=false, a late bt-agent start, service restart, or this migration's restart sets it true again. The panel observes neither PairableChanged nor agent registration, so no further write follows until open/close or adapter replacement. With default PairableTimeout=0 this is unbounded, and incoming requests again reach the new auto-accept agent outside a panel window. This directly undermines the claim to fix #7889. Make the consent state robust to agent (re)registration and readback rather than relying on a single QML load write.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (R1 state 1); corroboration

leads.summary: AuthorizeService admits untrusted, unpaired services outside the pairing window
leads.consequence: The comment says this unconditional acceptance is for bonded-device reconnects. BlueZ 5.87 queues service authorization for untrusted devices and calls Agent1.AuthorizeService without a paired/bonded predicate or Pairable check. Consequently an untrusted, unpaired device for which a service authorization is requested can be approved while the panel is closed. The old bluez-tools agent source checks Device.Paired and rejects unpaired requests. Preserve known-device reconnects but distinguish their service access from first-time untrusted devices; determine whether the shipped bluez-tools package uses the sampled implementation when contrasting old and new policy.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral Opus follow-up; confirmed in narrower form (never-paired acceptance, only sixaxis cable path by default); published as compact AuthorizeService note

leads.summary: Secondary Bluetooth adapters remain pairable and satisfy the global agent gate
leads.consequence: The panel writes Pairable only to Bluetooth.defaultAdapter. Quickshell exposes additional adapters, and BlueZ enables bondability across all controllers when the default agent registers. With two adapters, the secondary remains Pairable=true even if the primary is cleared on panel close; any_adapter_pairable() accepts the request whenever either adapter reports true. A request from an incoming device on the secondary can thus get Just Works authorization while every panel is closed. Check the requesting device path's adapter rather than any adapter, and close/manage all applicable adapter consent windows.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (state 2, scenario C); corroboration

leads.summary: Late BlueZ startup leaves this new agent skipped for the session
leads.consequence: The preexisting ExecCondition skips rather than fails a start when bluetooth.service has not become active. A user manager starting first can leave the unit inactive, so the new pairing agent never registers even after BlueZ and the panel appear; Restart=on-failure does not retry a skipped activation. The current test explicitly demands this line, and open #13258 addresses this startup boundary but conflicts with the changed unit and its tests. Existing behavior retained, but relevant to whether this PR provides device-initiated pairing on typical startup/hotplug paths.
leads.triage: pre-existing ExecCondition skip, unchanged by PR; dropped

leads.summary: Related pairing PRs conflict on bond handling and can regress the new connect-time bond path
leads.consequence: Open #7880 changes the same pair block to trust and connect only on successful `pair`, whereas this PR intentionally connects after a failed/timed-out pair to allow a bond initiated during `connect`. The open PR's successful-pair fixture expects trust without checking Bonded; this PR refuses it until bonded. Their model/test changes also disagree over whether a trusted-only device is in PAIRED. Open #11198 temporarily raises Pairable for `pair` and lowers it immediately before `connect`: if its write is kept on merge, this PR's intended peripheral-initiated bond during connect is blocked. Both pairs of heads are diverged, not stacked; merging needs semantic reconciliation, not a mechanical conflict resolution that drops one path.

leads.summary: Trusted-only unbonded devices still display as PAIRED, despite the changed click action
leads.consequence: The changed connectDevice() correctly routes a trusted-but-unbonded device through `pair` rather than `connect`, but the unchanged model still places that device under the PAIRED/known list; its test even asserts a trusted-only Mouse belongs there. Users may think an unsuccessful bond succeeded, and while the panel is not discovering, the device remains in the PAIRED list instead of AVAILABLE. Adjust the shared classifier and the assertion as well as the action path; open #7880 already proposes that classifier change.
leads.triage: factual; #7880 and #11198 verified open and touching the same files; merged into related-PR note

leads.summary: Competing bt-agent unit PRs require incompatible ExecStart and startup assertions
leads.consequence: Open #13258 changes the startup guard and ExecStart to wait for BlueZ in a shell while retaining bluez-tools bt-agent; its tests reject the ExecCondition this PR's tests require. Open #11937 replaces ExecStart with a supervisor, while this PR's test requires exactly `/usr/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent`. Both have diverged heads and conflict on the unit; resolving to either other PR's literal start command drops this PR's new Just Works agent. Carry the startup recovery/supervision semantics over to the new agent if these fixes are combined.
leads.triage: factual check: bin/omarchy-file-select already imports gi and install/omarchy-base.packages lists python-gobject; not new to this PR; dropped

leads.summary: Open #9965 adds an incompatible agent at the same installed path
leads.consequence: Open #9965 also adds bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent and points bt-agent.service to it, but implements a KeyboardDisplay agent that forwards authorization/passkeys to the Bluetooth panel. This PR adds a NoInputNoOutput auto-accept agent with a different API and policy at exactly that path. Both heads are diverged and add/add conflict; accepting one path as-is silently discards the other's Bluetooth workflow. The panel-only UI changes in #9965 may merge textually, but without its agent side they cannot handle its prompts.
leads.triage: verified Model.js keeps trusted in known/PAIRED; classification pre-existing, low value; dropped (covered by #7880 mention)

leads.summary: The Pairable tests pass even if the new agent rejects all pairing and the panel never writes Pairable
leads.consequence: The newly added checks only grep for names and source snippets. In an isolated test copy, changing `if props.get("Pairable") is True:` to `if False and props.get("Pairable") is True:` and putting a return at the start of syncPairable left bluetooth-test.sh green. This is a plausible regression of the precise consent behavior this follow-up purports to fix. Add a synthetic BlueZ ObjectManager/Adapter1 D-Bus fixture and exercise registration, true/false/absent Pairable and state changes; also drive the QML lifecycle in an isolated shell environment when available.
leads.triage: factual; #13258 and #11937 verified open touching bt-agent.service; related-PR note

leads.summary: New Python GI runtime is listed in ISO defaults, not declared as an omarchy package dependency
leads.consequence: The new unconditional service binary imports gi, and omarchy's hard depends include neither python nor python-gobject, although the full default installation list does contain python-gobject. On an installation created from just the packages rather than the default ISO list, the user service can fail on startup with ModuleNotFoundError and Restart=on-failure will retry. Confirm the release packaging dependency closure (including omarchy-settings and quickshell) before treating this as a published-package failure; if closure has no GI provider, add a package dependency for the service's interpreter/bindings.
leads.triage: factual; #9965 verified open, adds bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent (summary 'Bridge BlueZ pairing prompts to the Bluetooth panel'); related-PR note

limits: No real system D-Bus, Bluetooth controller or desktop session accessed. Behavioural security conclusions use BlueZ 5.87 and Quickshell 28771c7 source, rather than hardware; #I1 timing can also be exercised against private synthetic BlueZ/Quickshell services by the main reviewer.

Bluez-tools source inspected at f653217, not definitively the release pinned by Arch's bluez-tools package; the contrast with its old AuthorizeService behaviour should be rechecked at the shipped tag.

Merged overlapping PRs contain textual conflicts, so their final combination and test outcomes require human conflict resolution. No merged-code test was claimed for those conflicted versions; checked original test suite and current base tip in review.py.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12897#issuecomment-5779232177) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12897#issuecomment-5841820561), checked at `87c21cf5`.

**Resolved:** "Existing sessions keep the old rejecting agent". [`migrations/1790385200.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/migrations/1790385200.sh) reloads the user manager and restarts `bt-agent.service` only when it is active.

**Partly addressed:** "Auto-accept is not restricted to the claimed pairing window". The agent now rejects pairing requests when no adapter is Pairable, and the panel clears Pairable on the default adapter when it loads and closes. Pairable can still be on with every panel closed in three states, described below. Turning Pairable off also has a new side effect: pairing started outside the panel no longer bonds.

**Verified:** the agents at both heads, called as bluetoothd would call them, against a synthetic BlueZ on a private D-Bus (device under `hci0`):

| Adapter state | Previous head `898dad1a` | Current head `87c21cf5` |
|---|---|---|
| No adapter Pairable | all pairing requests accepted | all rejected; `AuthorizeService` accepted |
| `hci0` Pairable | accepted | accepted |
| Only `hci1` Pairable | accepted | **accepted** |
| `GetManagedObjects` fails | accepted | all rejected (fails closed) |

"Pairing requests" means `RequestAuthorization`, `RequestConfirmation`, `RequestPinCode` and `RequestPasskey`. With a stub `systemctl`, run under `bash -euo pipefail` like `omarchy-migrate`, the migration:
- exits 0 without a user manager;
- exits 1 (so it is retried) when the manager socket exists but does not respond, or when the reload, the state check or the restart fails;
- leaves an inactive, activating or failed unit alone;
- restarts an active unit after `daemon-reload`.

## Pairable can still be on with every panel closed

In Omarchy, only the panel clears Pairable, and only on its own load, open and close events ([`Panel.qml:442-449`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml#L442-L449), [`:586-609`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml#L586-L609)). It does not react when Pairable changes. BlueZ 5.87 sets Pairable on again by itself on every adapter whenever an agent registers as the default agent, because `AlwaysPairable` defaults to false and Omarchy does not change it (`src/agent.c:139-151`, `src/adapter.c:9152-9167`). The agent accepts if *any* adapter is Pairable ([`omarchy-bluetooth-agent:63-89`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent#L63-L89)).

```text
1. Agent restarts after the shell has loaded
   panel load clears Pairable -> bt-agent restarts -> BlueZ sets Pairable on -> no panel handler
   Triggers: this PR's migration run from the login notification or a manual omarchy-migrate,
   Restart=on-failure, a manual restart. (omarchy update restarts the shell afterwards, which
   clears it again, unless that restart is refused, for example while the session is locked.)
2. Two adapters
   BlueZ raises Pairable on every adapter -> panel clears only Bluetooth.defaultAdapter
   -> hci1 stays Pairable -> agent accepts requests for devices on hci0 as well (table above)
3. Bluetooth widget not in the bar (removed from the layout, plugin disabled, replacement bar)
   nothing ever clears Pairable for the session
```

The agent's decision covers LE Just Works and PIN/passkey pairing. For Classic devices without a stored key, the kernel accepts SSP bonding by itself whenever Pairable is on, as it did at the base. Source reading of the kernel and bluetoothd also limits who can reach these requests: links the host makes or accepts (known devices, devices the user connects to), not arbitrary nearby devices. No over-the-air test was done.

**Impact:** in these states, pairing is not limited to the time a panel is open. That is the guarantee the agent header and unit comment describe and the new #7889 claim relies on. The #7889 reproduction on the default controller (open the panel, close it, `bluetoothctl show`) should now report `Pairable: no`. In state 3, device-initiated LE Just Works changes from rejected at the base to accepted for the whole session.

**Suggested change:** let the always-running agent own the closed default. After `RegisterAgent`/`RequestDefaultAgent` and whenever an `Adapter1` appears, set Pairable false on every adapter. Gate each request on the Pairable of the requesting device's own adapter (its object path or `Device1.Adapter`), not on any adapter. The panel then only raises Pairable while open. A finite `PairableTimeout` would bound any remaining leak, though the panel would then need to refresh it while open.

## Pairing started outside the panel no longer bonds

When the adapter is not Pairable, the kernel removes bonding even from pairing the host starts: Classic in `net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:5339-5341`, LE in `smp.c:635-641`. bluetoothd's `Pair()` does not check Pairable. At the base, Pairable stayed on while `bt-agent` was registered. Now it is off whenever no panel is open.

```text
Pairable off (panel closed)
  bluetoothctl pair / omarchy-bluetooth-device pair from a terminal
  -> pairing completes without bonding -> wait_for_bond fails -> no trust
  -> the pairing is dropped on disconnect
```

The panel's own Pair action is affected the same way if the panel is closed before the device bonds. `omarchy-bluetooth-device pair` can run for about 55 s of timeouts or longer, and its comment notes that some peripherals bond only during `connect`. [#11198](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11198) describes this failure mode.

**Impact:** pairing from a terminal or another tool with no panel open, which bonded at the base, now leaves a device that has to be paired again after each disconnect. This comes from source reading; it was not run.

**Suggested change:** raise Pairable for the duration of a host-initiated pair in `omarchy-bluetooth-device` and restore it afterwards, as #11198 does. That also covers closing the panel mid-pair.

**`AuthorizeService`:** the author's reasoning holds for reconnects, because BlueZ asks the agent only about untrusted devices (`src/adapter.c:7783-7786`). The new agent accepts every device ([`omarchy-bluetooth-agent:115-118`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent#L115-L118)), while the base agent accepted only devices with `Paired: yes` (bluez-tools `src/lib/agent-helper.c:67-79`, the commit Arch's `bluez-tools 0.2.0-6` builds). With BlueZ and PipeWire defaults, the only extra path found is sixaxis USB cable pairing, which needs physical access and may be wanted. Source only. If the intent is bonded reconnects only, as the code comment states, a `Bonded` check matches it; it would also keep rejecting cable-paired sixaxis controllers, as the base did.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/bluetooth-test.sh` still passes with the agent's Pairable check deleted, and separately with `syncPairable()` changed to never write `false`. A test that calls the agent over a private D-Bus, like the table above, would catch the first; the second needs a check of the panel's Pairable writes.

**Migration file mode:** `1790385200.sh` is committed as `100755`; [`agents/skills/migrations.md:123-124`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/87c21cf5edde72812785b00aca80ec829d1555e7/agents/skills/migrations.md#L123-L124) requires `0644`. Harmless at runtime.

**Related open PRs:**
- [#9965](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9965) adds a different agent (it forwards pairing prompts to the panel) at the same `bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent` path and changes the same unit.
- [#11198](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11198) raises Pairable in `omarchy-bluetooth-device` during `pair` and restores it afterwards.
- [#7880](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/7880) also changes how trusted-only devices are handled, in `omarchy-bluetooth-device`, `Model.js` and `Panel.qml`.
- [#13258](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13258) and [#11937](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11937) change `bt-agent.service`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up limited to the Pairable gate, the panel's Pairable handling, `AuthorizeService` and the new migration. The current and previous agents ran against a synthetic BlueZ on a private D-Bus; the migration ran with a stub `systemctl`. The repository Bluetooth and systemd suites pass at the current head. BlueZ 5.87, Linux 7.2, Quickshell 0.3.1 and bluez-tools behaviour is source-derived, including the bonding finding. No real Bluetooth hardware, bluetoothd, over-the-air pairing or rendered panel was tested; the synthetic BlueZ does not reproduce BlueZ's own Pairable changes.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
